chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Saeed ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
You give him from the zakat until you enrich him.
ai.seo_question: How much zakat should be given to a poor person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the upper limit of zakat distribution, emphasizing that the giver should provide enough to achieve 'ghina' (financial independence) rather than merely sustaining temporary poverty. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view of zakat as a tool for social mobility and economic self-reliance, distinguishing it from general charity (sadaqah) which may be given in smaller, recurring amounts. The hadith reflects the practical application of Quranic verses on purification, ensuring the recipient is lifted out of the state of need entirely.
